scope: Proposition 9.2 (Retained-layer cost) of the manuscript “The sharp exponential rate of singularity for symmetric Bernoulli matrices” (preprints/The-sharp-exponential-rate-of-singularity-for-symmetric-Bernoulli-matrices-October-3-2026/symmetric-bernoulli-singularity.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 239 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8dfe5c0b8a0ca85c), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 50. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Typically for nonsingular binary matrices C of size m ∈ IN , the following estimate holds. Let h ∈ {1, 2} and let v1, . . . , vh be independent uniform columns in {0, 1}m, conditionally on C. Starting with G(0) = GC, let G(j) be the quotient of G(j−1) by the image of vj. For each 1 ≤ j ≤ h, and conditionally on any values of the preceding columns, Pr     X (p,e) retained in G(j−1)↠G(j) νp ≥ σ C, v1, . . . , vj−1     ≤ 2−Nσ/2 . (9.11) The typical set imposes one fixed precision on C, independent of the values of the preceding columns. When these columns occur in a random enlargement of C, no nonsingularity assumption on the destination matrix is required.
